title: The Bad winter that year
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：bad　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bad 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the painter wrote of ① a bad winter that year in the catalogue, and everybody in the studio said at once that it was ② worse than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the painter, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the bad ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the worst winter that year anybody in the studio had ever seen, or so the catalogue for May 1983 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too bad to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the bad ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the brush at the far easel, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a bad cold in the chest, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as bad as the cold in the chest they had once had in the old studio. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was bad or not, and he said so.

By 1996 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the catalogue. What the line asked for was ⑦ something bad, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next studio called the whole plan ⑧ quite bad; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the catalogue kept the names of the bad ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1999, in silence, she wrote of another bad winter that year in the same catalogue, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ worse than anybody had expected. ⑩ The worst cold in the chest in the whole studio, she said in 2001, was the one she could never quite name; the bad ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 坏（前置定语 a bad winter that year：1989 年画师在展品目录里记下的那件坏的冬天）
B. adj. 坏／严重（比较级 worse than：文中两处，一处比那年的冬天，一处比预想）
C. adj. 坏／严重（最高级 the worst：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 坏（表语 too bad to do：母亲觉得它太坏，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 严重（前置定语 a bad cold in the chest：叔叔把整件事称作一桩严重的寒疾）
F. adj. 严重（同级比较 as bad as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩胸口的寒疾相比）
G. adj. 严重（后置定语 something bad：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 严重（受程度副词修饰 quite bad：那位观者的评价）

items.q: the worst winter that year anybody
a bad cold in the chest
The worst cold in the chest in

answers.why: bad 意为“坏”，1989 年画师在展品目录里记下的是“一件坏的冬天”，此处作前置定语 a bad winter that year。
bad 意为“坏”，此处用比较级 worse than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
bad 意为“坏”，展品目录上 五月 那行字说它是画室里最坏的一件，故用最高级 the worst winter that year。
bad 意为“坏”，母亲认为这件东西“太坏了，谁也用不上”，too bad to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
bad 意为“严重”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩严重的寒疾”，此处作前置定语 a bad cold in the chest。
bad 意为“严重”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩胸口的寒疾一样严重”，同级比较用 as bad as。
bad 意为“严重”，展品目录上那半行字要的是“严重的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something bad。
bad 意为“严重”，邻画室来的那位观者认为这套计划“相当严重”，quite 修饰原级 bad。
bad 意为“严重”，1999 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要严重”，故用比较级 worse than。
bad 意为“严重”，母亲 2001 年说的是“整个画室里最严重的那一桩”，故用最高级 the worst cold in the chest。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1989 年，画师在展品目录里记下了一件坏的冬天。（a bad winter that year）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更坏。（worse than …）
母亲觉得它太坏，谁也用不上。（too bad to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩严重的寒疾。（a bad cold in the chest）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩胸口的寒疾一样严重。（as bad as …）
到了 1996 年，展品目录上只剩半行字：要的是一件严重的东西。（something bad）
answers: In 1989 the painter wrote of a bad winter that year in the catalogue.
Everybody said it was worse than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too bad to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a bad cold in the chest.
He said nobody would call it as bad as the cold in the chest they had once had.
By 1996 the catalogue asked for nothing but something bad.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 bad 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1989 the painter wrote of a bad winter that year in the catalogue, and nobody forgot it.
It was the worst winter that year in the studio, or so the catalogue says.
My mother thought it too bad to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a bad cold in the chest, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next studio called the plan quite bad, and everybody laughed.
The bad ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
